title.en: Volume 28: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, Yu Yeyan, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, Gu Bi, Zhang Li
title.raw: 卷28 和跋 奚牧 莫題 庾業延 賀狄乾 李栗 劉潔 古弼 張黎 Volume 28: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, Yu Yeyan, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, Gu Bi, Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 和跋 奚牧 莫題 庾業延 賀狄干 李栗 劉潔 古弼 張黎

translations.literal: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, Yu Yeyan, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, Gu Bi, Zhang Li
translations.idiomatic: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, Yu Yeyan, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, Gu Bi, and Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 和跋，代人也，世領部落，為國附臣。

translations.literal: He Ba was a man of Dai; for generations his clan had led the tribe and served as an attached subject of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba came from Dai. His line had led their tribe for generations as vassals of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 跋以才辯知名，太祖擢為外朝大人，參軍國大謀，雅有智算。

translations.literal: Ba was famed for talent in debate; Taizu raised him to outer-court grandee, had him take part in the state's great counsels, and he was by nature skilled in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Ba won renown for eloquence and wit. Taizu made him an outer-court grandee and drew him into the realm's weightiest counsels; he had a gift for calculation and design.

sentences.zh: 頻使稱旨，拜龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: On repeated missions he hit the mark of the ruler's intent and was appointed General of Dragon Agility.
translations.idiomatic: Mission after mission pleased the throne, and he was named General of Dragon Agility.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜爵日南公。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted the title Duke of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he received the title Duke of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，以功進為尚書，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Central Plains; for merit he was advanced to Master of Writing and stationed to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He marched in the pacification of the Central Plains and, for his service, was promoted to Master of Writing and set to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容德使兄子和守滑臺，和長史李辨殺和，求援於跋。

translations.literal: Murong De sent his elder brother's son He to hold Huatai; He's chief clerk Li Bian killed He and sought aid from Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De had his brother's son He defend Huatai. He's chief clerk, Li Bian, murdered him and appealed to Ba for rescue.

sentences.zh: 跋率輕騎赴之。

translations.literal: Ba led light cavalry to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: Ba rode at the head of light cavalry to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 既至，辨悔，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: When he had arrived, Bian repented and shut the gates to refuse and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ba arrived, Bian regretted his move, barred the gates, and held the city against him.

sentences.zh: 跋使尚書郎鄧暉說之，辨乃開門。

translations.literal: Ba sent Masters of Writing gentleman Deng Hui to persuade him, and Bian then opened the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Ba sent Deng Hui of the Masters of Writing to reason with him, and Bian at last opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 跋入，收其府藏。

translations.literal: Ba entered and seized the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: Ba entered the city and took possession of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 德聞之，遣將率三千騎，擊跋。

translations.literal: De heard of it and sent a general leading three thousand horsemen to strike Ba.
translations.idiomatic: When De learned of it, he dispatched a general with three thousand horsemen to attack Ba.

sentences.zh: 跋逆擊，大破之，擒其將士千餘人而還。

translations.literal: Ba met the attack head-on, routed them utterly, and returned having captured more than a thousand of their officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Ba met them head-on and broke their force, then withdrew with more than a thousand captives among officers and men.

sentences.zh: 於是陳潁之民，多來向化。

translations.literal: Thereupon many of the people of Chen and Ying came to submit and be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: After that, multitudes from Chen and Ying turned toward Wei rule.

sentences.zh: 改封定陵公。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 與常山王遵率眾五萬，討賀蘭部別帥木易于，破之。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Changshan, Zun, he led fifty thousand men to campaign against Muyi Yu, a separate chieftain of the Helan tribe, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He and the Prince of Changshan, Zun, took fifty thousand men against Muyi Yu, a splinter chief of the Helan, and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 出為平原太守。

translations.literal: He went out and became Grand Warden of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as grand warden of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖寵遇跋，冠於諸將。

translations.literal: Taizu favored and met with Ba; among the generals he stood at the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu showered favor on Ba above every other commander.

sentences.zh: 時羣臣皆敦尚恭儉，而跋好修虛譽，眩曜於時，性尤奢淫，太祖戒之，弗革。

translations.literal: At the time the ministers all honored and prized respectful frugality, yet Ba loved to cultivate empty reputation and dazzle the age; his nature was especially extravagant and dissolute. Taizu admonished him, but he did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: While the court cultivated sober humility, Ba courted hollow glory and flaunted his splendor before the age. He was by nature given to excess. Taizu warned him, yet he would not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 後車駕北狩豺山，收跋，刑之路側。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north at Jackal Mountain, Ba was seized and executed by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a northern hunt at Jackal Mountain, the emperor had Ba seized and put to death beside the road.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏自殺以從。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Liu, killed herself to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Liu, took her own life to follow him in death.

sentences.zh: 初，將刑跋，太祖命其諸弟毗等視訣，跋謂毗曰：「灅北地瘠，可居水南，就耕良田，廣為產業，各相勉勵，務自纂修。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ba was about to be executed, Taizu ordered his younger brothers Pi and the rest to witness the farewell; Ba told Pi: "The land north of Zei is poor soil—you may dwell south of the waters, take up cultivation on rich fields, broaden your estates, each urge the other on, and strive to build yourselves up.
translations.idiomatic: Before the execution Taizu had Ba's brothers, Pi among them, come for a final parting. Ba told Pi, "The country north of Zei is thin. Settle south of the river, farm the good land, build your holdings wide, and press one another to better your houses.

sentences.zh: 」令之背己曰：「汝曹何忍視吾之死也！

translations.literal: " He then turned his back on them and said: "How can you bear to watch me die!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he turned from them and cried, "How can you stand by and watch me die!"

sentences.zh: 」毗等解其微意，詐稱使者，云奔長安，追之不及。

translations.literal: Pi and the others grasped his subtle intent; they falsely claimed to be envoys, saying they were fleeing to Chang'an, and pursued him but could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and his brothers caught his hidden meaning. They pretended to be messengers bound for Chang'an and gave chase, but could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，遂誅其家。

translations.literal: Taizu was enraged and thereupon executed the whole family.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu flew into rage and put the entire house to the sword.

sentences.zh: 後世祖西巡五原，回幸犲山校獵，忽遇暴風，雲霧四塞。

translations.literal: Later Shizu on a western tour to Wuyuan turned back to hunt at Jackal Mountain, when suddenly a violent wind arose and clouds and mist closed in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Shizu toured the west as far as Wuyuan, then returned to hunt at Jackal Mountain. A sudden gale rose; cloud and mist walled the sky on every hand.

sentences.zh: 世祖怪而問之，羣下僉言跋世居此土，祠冢猶存，其或者能致斯變。

translations.literal: Shizu found it strange and questioned them; the assembled ministers all said that Ba for generations had dwelt on this soil, that his shrine tomb still stood, and that perhaps he could bring about such a change.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marveled and asked what it meant. The court together declared that Ba's line had long held this land, that his ancestral shrine still stood, and that he might have stirred this omen.

sentences.zh: 帝遣建興公古弼祭以三牲，霧即除散。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Gu Bi, Duke of Jianxing, to offer sacrifice with the three sacrificial beasts; the mist at once dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gu Bi, Duke of Jianxing, to sacrifice with the triple offering of ox, sheep, and pig. The fog lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 後世祖蒐狩之日，每先祭之。

translations.literal: Afterward, on days when Shizu went hunting, he always sacrificed to Ba first.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever Shizu took the field on a hunt, he made offering to Ba before all else.

sentences.zh: 少子歸，從征赫連昌有功，拜統萬將軍，賜爵成皐男。

translations.literal: His youngest son Gui, in campaigning against Helian Chang with merit, was appointed General of Tongwan and granted the title Baron of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Gui earned merit against Helian Chang, was made General of Tongwan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 與西平公安頡攻虎牢，拔之。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Xiping, Anji, he attacked Hulao and took it.
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince of Xiping, Anji, he stormed Hulao and captured it.

sentences.zh: 進爵高陽侯。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Marquis of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Marquis of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 後以罪徙配涼州為民。

translations.literal: Later, for a crime he was banished and assigned to Liang Province as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, condemned for a crime, he was exiled to common status in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳作亂於關中，復拜歸龍驤將軍往討之。

translations.literal: When Gai Wu rebelled in Guanzhong, Gui was again appointed Dragon Agile General and sent to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Wu rose in revolt in Guanzhong, Gui was again named Dragon Agile General and sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜使持節、冠軍將軍、雍城鎮都大將、高陽侯。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Champion General, Grand Commander of the Garrison at Yongcheng, and Marquis of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received the staff of authority as champion general, grand commander of the Yongcheng garrison, and Marquis of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He came to his end.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子度，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Du inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 尚書都官郎、昌平太守。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Bureau of Punishments, and Grand Warden of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman in the Masters of Writing, bureau of punishments, and as grand warden of Changping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He expired.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 度子延穆，司州部郡從事，早卒。

translations.literal: Du's son Yanmu was a clerk in the commandery offices of Si Province and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Yanmu held a clerkship in the Si Province commanderies and died in his prime.

sentences.zh: 子安，武定末，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son An, at the end of the Wuding era, was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son An, in the last years of Wuding, served as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 奚牧，代人也，重厚有智謀。

translations.literal: Xi Mu was a man of Dai, grave and steady, with wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mu came from Dai—steady, weighty in counsel, and shrewd in design.

sentences.zh: 太祖寵遇之，稱之曰仲兄。

translations.literal: Taizu favored and met with him and called him his second elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu favored him warmly and addressed him as a second elder brother.

sentences.zh: 初，劉顯謀害太祖，梁眷知其謀，潛使牧與穆崇至七介山以告，語在崇傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Xian plotted to harm Taizu, Liang Juan learned of the plot and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Qijie Mountain to report it—the account is in Chong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian once plotted against Taizu's life, Liang Juan uncovered the scheme and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Qijie Mountain to warn him—the full tale stands in Chong's biography.

sentences.zh: 太祖錄先帝舊臣，又以牧告顯之功，拜為治民長，敷奏政事，參與計謀。

translations.literal: Taizu recorded the old ministers of the former emperor, and because Mu had reported Xian's plot he was appointed Chief Who Governs the People, presented and played out government affairs, and took part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu honored the veterans of the former reign and, for Mu's warning against Xian, made him chief who governs the people, set him to frame and present policy, and drew him into counsel.

sentences.zh: 太祖征慕容寶，加輔國將軍，略地晉川，獲寶丹陽王買得及離石護軍高秀和於平陶。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Murong Bao he was added as General Who Supports the State; he overran the Jin region and at Pingtao captured Bao's Prince of Danyang, Maid, and the Protector of the Army of Lishi, Gao Xiuhe.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaign against Murong Bao, Mu was named general who supports the state. He swept the Jin territories and at Pingtao took Bao's Prince of Danyang, Maid, together with Gao Xiuhe, protector of the army at Lishi.

sentences.zh: 以軍功拜并州刺史，賜爵任城公。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Regional Inspector of Bing and granted the title Duke of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his victories he was made regional inspector of Bing and enfeoffed Duke of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 州與姚興接界，興頗寇邊，牧乃與興書，稱頓首，鈞禮抗之，責興侵邊不直之意。

translations.literal: The province bordered Yao Xing's domain; Xing often raided the frontier. Mu then wrote to Xing, styling himself with forehead to ground and using the balanced epistolary form to resist him, reproaching Xing for the injustice of invading the border.
translations.idiomatic: Bing shared a border with Yao Xing, who raided often. Mu wrote to him in the full forms of submission—forehead to earth, balanced courtesy—yet turned the letter into a rebuke of Xing's border raids as unjust.

sentences.zh: 興以與國通和，恨之。

translations.literal: Xing, because the state was in communication and alliance, hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, bound to Wei by treaty, took the letter as an outrage.

sentences.zh: 有言於太祖，太祖戮之。

translations.literal: Someone spoke of it to Taizu, and Taizu executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Taizu, and he had Mu put to death.

sentences.zh: 莫題，代人也，多智有才用。

translations.literal: Mo Ti was a man of Dai, of much wisdom and with talent for use.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ti came from Dai—clever, resourceful, and fit for command.

sentences.zh: 初為幢將，領禁兵。

translations.literal: At first he was a standard-bearer general and led the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as standard-bearer general in charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖之征慕容寶也，寶夜來犯營，車人驚駭。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Murong Bao, Bao came by night to attack the camp and the chariot soldiers were thrown into terror.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's campaign against Murong Bao, Bao struck the camp by night and the army fell into panic.

sentences.zh: 遂有亡還京師者，言官軍敗於栢肆，京師不安。

translations.literal: Thereupon some fled back to the capital, saying the government army had been defeated at Baixi; the capital was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Runners carried word to the capital that the imperial army had been broken at Baixi, and the city trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 南安公元順因之欲攝國事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nan'an, Yuan Shun, took advantage of this and wished to seize control of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Nan'an, Yuan Shun, seized on the alarm and moved to take the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 題謂順曰：「此大事，不可輕爾，宜審待後要，不然禍將及矣。

translations.literal: Ti said to Shun: "This is a great matter and cannot be treated lightly; you should carefully await later developments—otherwise disaster will reach you.
translations.idiomatic: Ti told Shun, "This is no small matter. Do not act rashly. Wait until the truth is clear—otherwise ruin will find you.

sentences.zh: 」順乃止。

translations.literal: " Shun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun held back.

sentences.zh: 以功拜平遠將軍，賜爵扶柳公，進號左將軍，改為高邑公。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, granted the title Duke of Foliu, advanced in title to Left General, and changed to Duke of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was named general who pacifies the distance, enfeoffed Duke of Foliu, raised to left general, and then made Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 出除中山太守，督司州之山東七郡事。

translations.literal: He went out and was removed to Grand Warden of Zhongshan, supervising the seven commanderies east of the mountains in Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as grand warden of Zhongshan, with oversight of the seven eastern commanderies of Si Province beyond the Taihang.

sentences.zh: 車駕征姚興，次於晉陽，而上黨羣盜秦頗、丁零翟都等聚眾於壺關，詔題帥眾三千以討之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Yao Xing it halted at Jinyang; bandits of Shangdang—Qin Po of the masses and Zhai Du of the Dingling—gathered their followers at Huguan. An edict ordered Ti to command three thousand men to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor campaigned against Yao Xing and paused at Jinyang, brigands of Shangdang—Qin Po among the people and the Dingling leader Zhai Du—raised bands at Huguan. Ti was ordered to take three thousand men against them.

sentences.zh: 上黨太守捕頗，斬之。

translations.literal: The Grand Warden of Shangdang captured Po and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The grand warden of Shangdang seized Po and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 都走林慮。

translations.literal: Du fled to Linlu.
translations.idiomatic: Du fled into the hills at Linlu.

sentences.zh: 詔題搜山窮討，盡平之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ti to search the mountains and pursue to the end, and he pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was commanded to comb the mountains and hunt them down to the last man until the region was quiet.

sentences.zh: 初，昭成末，太祖季父窟咄徙于長安。

translations.literal: In the last years of Zhaocheng, Taizu's younger paternal uncle Kudou was moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the reign of Emperor Zhaocheng, Taizu's uncle Kudou was resettled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 苻堅敗，從慕容永東遷。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, he followed Murong Yong east in migration.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's fall he marched east with Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 及永自立，以窟咄為新興太守。

translations.literal: When Yong declared himself ruler, he made Kudou Grand Warden of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong took the throne, he appointed Kudou grand warden of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 登國初，劉顯遣弟亢埿等迎窟咄，寇南鄙。

translations.literal: At the opening of Dengguo, Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kanghou and others to welcome Kudou, and they raided the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dengguo, Liu Xian sent his brother Kanghou and others to bring Kudou home, and they harried the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 題時貳於太祖，遺箭於窟咄，謂之曰「三歲犢豈勝重載」，言窟咄長而太祖少也。

translations.literal: At the time Ti was disloyal to Taizu; he sent an arrow to Kudou, telling him, "Can a three-year-old calf bear a heavy load?"—meaning Kudou was elder and Taizu young.
translations.idiomatic: Ti then stood against Taizu and sent Kudou an arrow with the message, "Can a calf of three years bear a heavy load?"—telling him the uncle was the elder strength and the nephew still a boy.

sentences.zh: 太祖既銜之。

translations.literal: Taizu thereafter harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu never forgave the insult.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年，有告題居處倨傲，擬則人主。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianci, someone reported that Ti in his dwelling was haughty and arrogant, taking the demeanor of a sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianci, an informer accused Ti of living in insolent state, matching his manner to a ruler's.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃使人示之箭，告之曰：「三歲犢，能勝重載不？

translations.literal: Taizu then had someone show him the arrow and tell him: "A three-year-old calf—can it bear a heavy load or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had the arrow brought before him and asked, "A calf of three years—can it bear a heavy load?"

sentences.zh: 」題奉詔，父子對泣，詰朝乃刑之。

translations.literal: Ti received the edict; father and son faced each other weeping, and on the morrow he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ti took the decree. He and his son wept face to face through the night. At dawn they led him to execution.

sentences.zh: 庾業延，代人也，後賜名岳。

translations.literal: Yu Yeyan was a man of Dai; later he was granted the name Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yeyan came from Dai and was later granted the personal name Yue.

sentences.zh: 其父及兄和辰，世典畜牧。

translations.literal: His father and his elder brother He Chen for generations managed the royal herds.
translations.idiomatic: His father and elder brother He Chen had for generations overseen the imperial herds.

sentences.zh: 稍轉中部大人。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to grandee of the central tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to grandee of the central tribes.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩，氐寇內侮。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng passed away, the Di raided within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaocheng died, Di forces raided across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 事難之間，收斂畜產，富擬國君。

translations.literal: Amid the troubles he gathered in livestock and wealth until his riches rivaled the ruler's.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil he rounded up herds and stores until his wealth rivaled the throne's own.

sentences.zh: 劉顯謀逆，太祖外幸，和辰奉獻明太后歸太祖，又得其資用。

translations.literal: When Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Taizu went out on campaign; He Chen presented Empress Dowager Ming to Taizu and also supplied him with resources.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian plotted treason and Taizu marched abroad, He Chen escorted Empress Dowager Ming back to him and furnished the army with supplies.

sentences.zh: 以和辰為內侍長。

translations.literal: He Chen was made Chief of the Inner Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He Chen was appointed chief of the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 和辰分別公私舊畜，頗不會旨，太祖由是恨之。

translations.literal: He Chen divided the old herds of public and private stock and largely missed the mark of the ruler's intent; Taizu therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He Chen's division of the old herds between public and private stock missed Taizu's intent, and the emperor came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 岳獨恭慎修謹，善處危難之間，太祖喜之。

translations.literal: Yue alone was respectful, cautious, and strict in conduct, skilled at handling intervals of peril; Taizu delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue alone was reverent, careful, and steady in crisis. Taizu took pleasure in him.

sentences.zh: 與王建等俱為外朝大人，參預軍國。

translations.literal: With Wang Jian and others he was alike made outer-court grandee and took part in army and state.
translations.idiomatic: He stood with Wang Jian and others among the outer-court grandees, sharing in military and civil counsel.

sentences.zh: 太祖既絕慕容垂，以岳為大人，使詣慕容永。

translations.literal: When Taizu had broken with Murong Chui, he made Yue a grandee and sent him to Murong Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu broke with Murong Chui, he named Yue a grandee and dispatched him to Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 永服其辭義。

translations.literal: Yong was convinced by his rhetoric and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was won over by his words.

sentences.zh: 垂圍永於長子，永告急求援，岳與陳留王虔以五萬騎東渡河救之，次於秀容，破山胡部高車門等，徙其部落。

translations.literal: When Chui besieged Yong at Changzi, Yong reported urgency and sought aid; Yue with the Prince of Chenliu, Qian, led fifty thousand horsemen east across the river to rescue him, halted at Xiurong, defeated the mountain Hu chieftain Gaochemen of the Gaoche tribe and others, and moved their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Chui besieged Yong at Changzi; Yong cried for help. Yue and the Prince of Chenliu, Qian, crossed the Yellow River at the head of fifty thousand horse, camped at Xiurong, broke the mountain Hu under the Gaoche chieftain Gaochemen, and resettled their clans.

sentences.zh: 會永滅，乃班師。

translations.literal: When Yong perished they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fell, they marched home.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，拜安遠將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Central Plains and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the Central Plains and was named general who pacifies the distance.

sentences.zh: 官軍之驚於栢肆也，賀蘭部帥附力眷、紇突隣部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根等聞之，聚黨反於陰館。

translations.literal: When the government army was thrown into alarm at Baixi, the Helan chieftain Fuli Juan, the Getunlin chieftain Niwuni, and the Hexi chieftain Chinugen and others heard of it and gathered their factions to rebel at Yinguan.
translations.idiomatic: When panic spread from the rout at Baixi, Fuli Juan of the Helan, Niwuni of the Getunlin, and Chinugen of the Hexi heard the news and raised their clans in revolt at Yinguan.

sentences.zh: 南安公元順討之，不克，死者數千人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nan'an, Yuan Shun, campaigned against them but could not overcome them; those who died numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Nan'an, Yuan Shun, marched against them and failed; thousands fell.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，詔岳率萬騎，還討叱奴根等，殄之，百姓乃安。

translations.literal: Taizu heard of it and ordered Yue to lead ten thousand horsemen back to campaign against Chinugen and the rest, exterminating them; the common people then were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Yue back at the head of ten thousand horse to crush Chinugen and his allies. The land grew calm again.

sentences.zh: 離石胡帥呼延鐵、西河胡帥張崇等不樂內徙，聚黨反叛。

translations.literal: The Hu chieftain of Lishi, Huyan Tie, and the Hu chieftain of Xihe, Zhang Chong, were unwilling to move within the borders; they gathered factions and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Tie, Hu chief of Lishi, and Zhang Chong of Xihe refused resettlement inland and rose with their bands.

sentences.zh: 岳率騎三千，討破之，斬鐵擒崇，搜山窮討，散其餘黨。

translations.literal: Yue led three thousand horsemen, campaigned and defeated them, beheaded Tie and captured Chong, searched the mountains and pursued to the end, and scattered the remainder of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took three thousand horse, broke their force, slew Tie and took Chong alive, combed the hills until no rebel remained, and broke up the rest of the band.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵西昌公，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Duke of Xichang and advanced in title to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: For these victories he was enfeoffed Duke of Xichang and promoted to general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又討反人張超、清河太守傅世，並破平。

translations.literal: He again campaigned against the rebel Zhang Chao and the Grand Warden of Qinghe, Fu Shi, and defeated and pacified them both.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again against the rebel Zhang Chao and Fu Shi, grand warden of Qinghe, and brought both campaigns to ruin.

sentences.zh: 以岳為鄴行臺。

translations.literal: Yue was made Mobile Court Commissioner at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was appointed mobile court commissioner at Ye.

sentences.zh: 岳為將有謀略，治軍清整，常以少擊多，士眾服其智勇，名冠諸將。

translations.literal: As a general he had stratagem; in governing the army he was clear and orderly; he constantly used the few to strike the many; officers and soldiers submitted to his wisdom and courage—his name stood at the crown among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In command he was a strategist; his camps were disciplined and clean. He made a habit of beating larger forces with smaller ones. The ranks bowed to his wit and daring, and among generals his name stood first.

sentences.zh: 及罷鄴行臺，以所統六郡置相州，即拜岳為刺史。

translations.literal: When the mobile court at Ye was abolished, the six commanderies he had governed were set up as Xiang Province, and he was at once appointed its regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ye mobile court was dissolved, his six commanderies became Xiang Province, and he was immediately made its inspector.

sentences.zh: 公廉平當，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: He was fair, incorrupt, and even-handed; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with fairness and clean hands, and the people spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 舊有園池，時果初熟，丞吏送之，岳不受，曰：「果未進御，吾何得先食？

translations.literal: Of old there were gardens and ponds; when the season's fruit first ripened, clerks and officials sent some; Yue would not accept them, saying: "The fruit has not yet been presented to the throne—how may I eat first?"
translations.idiomatic: He kept the old gardens and orchards. When the first fruit of the season ripened, his clerks brought him a basket. Yue refused it, saying, "Until fruit reaches the imperial table, how should I taste it first?"

sentences.zh: 」其謹如此。

translations.literal: His scrupulousness was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the strictness of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 後遷司空。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 岳兄子路有罪，諸父兄弟悉誅，特赦岳父子。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother's son Lu had committed a crime; all the paternal uncles and brothers were executed, but Yue and his son were specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's nephew Lu had offended; every uncle and brother was put to death, yet Yue and his son alone were spared.

sentences.zh: 天賜四年，詔賜岳舍地於南宮，岳將家僮治之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianci an edict granted Yue an estate in the Southern Palace; Yue led household servants to develop it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianci the court granted Yue a holding in the Southern Palace, and he set his household to work it.

sentences.zh: 候官告岳衣服鮮麗，行止風采，擬儀人君。

translations.literal: Surveillance officials reported that Yue's clothes were splendid and bright and that his bearing and deportment imitated a ruler's.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors reported that Yue dressed in bright finery and carried himself like a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 太祖時既不豫，多所猜惡，遂誅之。

translations.literal: When Taizu was unwell he was full of suspicion and had many men killed; Yue was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, already ill and suspicious, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 時人咸冤惜焉。

translations.literal: People of the time all considered it a wrongful death and mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it called it a wrongful death and grieved.

sentences.zh: 岳葬在代西善無之界。

translations.literal: Yue was buried on the border of Shanyin west of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was buried on the western border of Dai, at Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 後世祖討赫連氏，經其墓宅，愴然動容，遂下詔為立廟，令一州之民，四時致祭。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Helian; passing his tomb residence, he was moved to sorrow, issued an edict to build a temple, and ordered the people of one province to offer sacrifices in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against the Helian, Emperor Shizu passed his tomb, was moved to sorrow, ordered a temple built, and commanded one province to sacrifice in the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 求其子孫任為將帥者，得其子陵。

translations.literal: He sought descendants of Yue fit to serve as generals and found his son Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a descendant of Yue fit for command and found his son Ling.

sentences.zh: 從征有功，聽襲爵。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns with merit and was permitted to inherit the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ling followed campaigns with merit and was allowed to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 路，皇始初，從征慕容寶，為城門校尉。

translations.literal: Lu, at the beginning of Huangshi, followed the campaign against Murong Bao as Commandant of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, at the opening of Huangshi, marched against Murong Bao as commandant of the city gates.

sentences.zh: 遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 爵高平公而誅。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping and then executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping—and then executed.

sentences.zh: 賀狄干，代人也。

translations.literal: He Digan, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Digan was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 家本小族，世忠厚，為將以平當稱。

translations.literal: His family was originally of a small clan; for generations they were honest and steady, and as generals they were famed for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was small and for generations honest; as a commander he was famed for fairness.

sentences.zh: 稍遷北部大人。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand chief of the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與長孫嵩為對，明於聽察，為人愛敬。

translations.literal: At the founding of Dengguo he was paired with Zhangsun Song; clear in hearing and judgment, he was loved and respected by men.
translations.idiomatic: At the state's founding he was paired with Zhangsun Song—keen of ear and judgment, loved and respected.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣狄干致馬千匹，結婚於姚萇。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Digan to present a thousand horses and conclude a marriage with Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Digan with a thousand horses to seal marriage with Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 會萇死興立，因止狄干而絕婚。

translations.literal: Chang died and Xing took the throne; he therefore detained Digan and broke the betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Chang died; Xing detained Digan and broke the match.

sentences.zh: 興弟平率眾寇平陽，太祖討平之，擒其將狄伯支、唐小方等三十餘人。

translations.literal: Xing's younger brother Ping led troops to raid Pingyang; Taizu campaigned to pacify Ping and captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's brother Ping raided Pingyang; Taizu defeated him and took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and thirty more.

sentences.zh: [1]天賜中，詔北新侯安同送唐小方於長安。

translations.literal: [1] In Tianci, an edict that Marquis of Northern Xin An Tong escort Tang Xiaofang to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In Tianci an edict ordered An Tong, Marquis of Northern Xin, to escort Tang Xiaofang to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕社崘與興和親，送馬八千匹。

translations.literal: Later the Rouran She Lün allied with Xing in marriage and sent eight thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Rouran khan She Lün allied with Xing by marriage and sent eight thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 始濟河，赫連屈孑忿興與國交好，乃叛興，邀留社崘馬。

translations.literal: Just as they were crossing the river, Helian Qubing resented Xing's friendship with our state and rebelled against Xing, intercepting She Lün's horses.
translations.idiomatic: As they crossed the river, Helian Qubing, angered at Xing's friendship with us, rebelled and seized She Lün's horses.

sentences.zh: 興乃遣使，請以駿馬千匹贖伯支而遣狄干還。

translations.literal: Xing then sent envoys, offering a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and send Digan back.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then sent envoys offering a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and return Digan.

sentences.zh: 太祖意在離間二寇，於是許之。

translations.literal: Taizu wished to estrange the two enemies and therefore agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu meant to set the two foes against each other and agreed.

sentences.zh: 狄干在長安幽閉，因習讀書史，通論語、尚書諸經，舉止風流，有似儒者。

translations.literal: While confined in Chang'an, Digan studied histories and mastered the Analects, Documents, and other classics; his bearing was elegant, like a Confucian's.
translations.idiomatic: Confined in Chang'an he studied histories and the Analects and Documents; his bearing grew elegant, like a scholar's.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖普封功臣，狄干雖為姚興所留，遙賜爵襄武侯，加秦兵將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu enfeoffed the meritous in general, though Digan was detained by Yao Xing, he was granted from afar the title Marquis of Xiangwu and added General of Qin Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was rewarded, though Xing still held him, Digan was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and General of Qin Troops.

sentences.zh: 及狄干至，太祖見其言語衣服，有類羌俗，以為慕而習之，故忿焉，既而殺之。

translations.literal: When Digan arrived, Taizu saw his speech and clothes resembled Qiang custom; he thought Digan had admired and learned them, grew angry, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Digan returned, Taizu saw his speech and dress in Qiang fashion, thought him a mimic, grew angry, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 弟歸，亦剛直方雅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Gui was also upright and refined.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Gui was likewise upright and refined.

sentences.zh: 與狄干俱死。

translations.literal: He died together with Digan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui died with him.

sentences.zh: 李栗，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Li Li, a man of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li was from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，父祖入國。

translations.literal: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather came north.

sentences.zh: 少辯捷，有才能，兼有將略。

translations.literal: In youth he was eloquent and quick, with ability and also military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was quick and eloquent, gifted in arms as well as wit.

sentences.zh: 初隨太祖幸賀蘭部，在元從二十一人中。

translations.literal: At first he followed Taizu on his visit to the Helan tribe, among the twenty-one original followers.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Taizu to the Helan, one of the twenty-one original followers.

sentences.zh: 太祖愛其藝能。

translations.literal: Taizu loved his artistry.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu loved his skill.

sentences.zh: 時王業草創，爪牙心腹，多任親近，唯栗一介遠寄，兼非戚舊，當世榮之。

translations.literal: When the royal enterprise was still being founded, close aides were mostly kin; only Li was a lone man stationed far, not a relative by marriage — the age honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm was still being forged, confidants were kin; Li alone was a distant outsider, no in-law—men of the day held it an honor.

sentences.zh: 數有戰功，拜左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly had battle merit and was appointed Left Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He won battle after battle and was named left army general.

sentences.zh: 太祖征慕容寶，栗督五萬騎為前驅，軍之所至，莫不降下。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Murong Bao, Li commanded fifty thousand cavalry as vanguard; wherever the army went none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaign against Murong Bao, Li led fifty thousand horse as vanguard; every place the host reached submitted.

sentences.zh: 遷左將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left General.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to left general.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶棄中山東走也，栗以輕騎追之，不及而還。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao abandoned Zhongshan and fled east, Li pursued with light cavalry but did not overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao abandoned Zhongshan and fled east, Li rode light horse in pursuit, could not catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 栗性簡慢，矜寵，不率禮度，每在太祖前舒放倨傲，不自祗肅，咳唾任情。

translations.literal: Li was by nature blunt and arrogant, enjoying favor, not observing ritual; before Taizu he would stretch and act insolently without self-restraint, coughing and spitting as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li was blunt and arrogant, spoiled by favor, careless of ritual; before Taizu he lounged insolently, coughing and spitting at will.

sentences.zh: 太祖積其宿過，天興三年遂誅之。

translations.literal: Taizu accumulated his old faults; in the third year of Tianxing he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu tallied his old offenses; in the third year of Tianxing he was executed.

sentences.zh: 於是威嚴始厲，制勒羣下盡卑謙之禮，自栗始也。

translations.literal: Then authority grew stern; regulation of the host to observe humble courtesy began with Li.
translations.idiomatic: From then on majesty was enforced and the court taught humble courtesy—beginning with Li.

sentences.zh: 劉潔，長樂信都人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jie, a man of Xindu in Chang Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie was from Xindu in Chang Le.

sentences.zh: 祖父生，頗解卜筮。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng was skilled in divination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng was versed in divination.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，慕容氏來獻女，為公主家臣，仍隨入朝。

translations.literal: In Zhaocheng's time the Murong clan came to present a woman; he became household retainer of the princess and followed into court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's reign the Murong sent a princess; he became a household retainer and followed her into court.

sentences.zh: 賜以妻，生子。

translations.literal: He was granted a wife and a son was born.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a wife and had a son.

sentences.zh: 父提，太祖時，官至樂陵太守，賜爵信都男。

translations.literal: His father Ti, in Taizu's time reached Administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ti, under Taizu, rose to administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Ti died.

sentences.zh: 潔性強力多智，數從征討有功，進爵會稽公。

translations.literal: Jie was by nature forceful and intelligent; he repeatedly followed campaigns with merit and was advanced to Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was forceful and clever; he campaigned again and again with merit and was raised to Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 河西胡張外、建興王紹等聚黨為逆，潔與永安侯魏勤率眾三千人，屯于西河以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The Hexi Hu Zhang Wai, Jianxing King Shao, and others gathered factions in rebellion; Jie with Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin led three thousand troops stationed at Xihe to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wai of the Hexi Hu, Jianxing King Shao, and others raised factions; Jie with Wei Qin, Marquis of Yong'an, took three thousand men to garrison Xihe and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 又與勤及功勞將軍元屈等擊吐京叛胡。

translations.literal: He also with Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu attacked the rebellious Hu at Tujing.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu to strike the rebel Hu at Tujing.

sentences.zh: 時離石胡出以眷引屈丐騎，斷截山嶺邀潔，潔失馬，登山力戰，矢刃俱盡，為胡所執，送詣屈丐。

translations.literal: At the time Lishi Hu chief Chu Yijuan led Qubing's cavalry by way of Juan, cut off the mountain ridges to intercept Jie; Jie lost his horse, fought on the mountain with all his strength until arrows and blades were exhausted, was seized by the Hu and sent to Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chu Yijuan of the Lishi Hu led Qubing's horse by Juan, blocked the passes, and cut Jie off; Jie lost his mount, fought on foot until steel was spent, was taken, and sent to Qubing.

sentences.zh: 潔聲氣不撓，呼其字而與之言，神色自若。

translations.literal: Jie's voice and spirit did not waver; he called Qubing by his style name and spoke with him, his expression calm.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's voice never broke; he called Qubing by his style and spoke freely, his face unchanged.

sentences.zh: 屈丐壯而釋之。

translations.literal: Qubing admired him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing admired his spirit and let him go.

sentences.zh: 後得還國，典東部事。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the state and oversaw eastern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned and oversaw the eastern administration.

sentences.zh: 太宗寢疾，世祖監國，潔與古弼等選侍東宮，對綜機要，敷奏百揆。

translations.literal: When Taizong was ill, Shizu supervised the state; Jie with Gu Bi and others were selected to attend the Eastern Palace, handling critical affairs and presenting memorials on all departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong fell ill and Shizu oversaw the realm, Jie with Gu Bi and others were chosen to serve the Eastern Palace, handling secrets and reporting on every office.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以告反者，又獻直言，所在合旨，奇其有柱石之用，委以大任。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, reporting on rebels and offering blunt advice — wherever he spoke it matched intent; they marveled at his pillar-and-timber usefulness and entrusted great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he exposed rebels and spoke bluntly; his words always hit the mark, and the court, seeing a pillar of state, gave him heavy trust.

sentences.zh: 及議軍國，朝臣咸推其能。

translations.literal: When military and state affairs were discussed, court ministers all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: In council on war and state, every minister praised his capacity.

sentences.zh: 於是超遷尚書令，改為鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and changed to Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to director of the masters of writing and made Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 世祖破蠕蠕大檀于雲中，潔言於世祖曰：「大檀恃眾，雖破膽奔北，恐不懼往敗，將復送死。

translations.literal: When Shizu defeated the Rouran Dadan at Yunzhong, Jie said to Shizu: "Dadan relies on his numbers; though broken in spirit he flees north, I fear he does not dread past defeat and will come again to his death.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu broke the Rouran Dadan at Yunzhong, Jie told him, "Dadan still has his host; though routed north, he may not fear defeat and will return to die in battle.

sentences.zh: 請收田訖，復一大舉，東西並進，為二道討之。

translations.literal: I beg that after the harvest is gathered we mount another great campaign, advancing east and west in two columns to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gather the harvest, then strike again in force, east and west together."

sentences.zh: 」世祖然其言。

translations.literal: " Shizu approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 後大議征討，潔言宜先平馮跋，世祖不從。

translations.literal: Later in great deliberation on campaigns, Jie said Feng Bo should be pacified first; Shizu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Later, debating campaigns, Jie urged pacifying Feng Bo first; Shizu refused.

sentences.zh: 敕勒新民以將吏侵奪，咸出怨言，期牛馬飽草，當赴漠北。

translations.literal: The Tiele new subjects complained that officers and clerks seized from them; all murmured in resentment, setting a date when cattle and horses had eaten their fill on the grass to flee north to the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Tiele settlers complained that officers plundered them; murmurs spread, and they fixed a day—when the herds were fat on the grass—to flee north into the desert.

sentences.zh: 潔與左僕射安原奏，欲及河冰未解，徙之河西，冰解之後，不得北遁。

translations.literal: Jie with Left Vice Minister An Yuan memorialized, wishing to move them west of the river before the ice broke up, so that when the ice melted they could not flee north.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and An Yuan, left vice minister, urged moving them west of the river before the ice broke, so when it thawed they could not escape north.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Shizu said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "No.

sentences.zh: 此等習俗，放散日久，有似園中之鹿，急則衝突，緩之則定。

translations.literal: These people are long accustomed to wandering; they are like deer in a garden — pressed, they bolt; eased, they settle.
translations.idiomatic: They have wandered for generations, like deer in an enclosure—drive them hard and they stampede; ease them and they stay.

sentences.zh: 吾自處之有道，不煩徙也。

translations.literal: I myself have a way to handle them; there is no need to move them.
translations.idiomatic: I know how to govern them; no need to relocate."

sentences.zh: 」潔等固執，乃聽分徙三萬餘落於河西，西至白鹽池。

translations.literal: " Jie and the others insisted, and he then permitted relocating more than thirty thousand households west of the river, as far as White Salt Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Jie pressed on, and the emperor allowed more than thirty thousand households to be moved west of the river, as far as White Salt Marsh.

sentences.zh: 新民驚駭，皆曰：「圈我於河西之中，是將殺我也」，欲西走涼州。

translations.literal: The new subjects were alarmed and all said, "Penning us in the midst of Hexi is to kill us," and wished to flee west to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The settlers were terrified: "They have penned us in Hexi to slaughter us," and many meant to flee west to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 潔與侍中古弼屯五原河北，左僕射安原屯悅拔城北，備之。

translations.literal: Jie with Palace Attendant Gu Bi garrisoned north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan; An Yuan, Left Vice Minister, garrisoned north of Yueba city — to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie with Gu Bi, palace attendant, held the north bank at Wuyuan; An Yuan held north of Yueba—to block them.

sentences.zh: 既而新民數千騎北走，潔追討之。

translations.literal: Before long several thousand of the new subjects fled north on horseback; Jie pursued and attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thousands fled north on horse; Jie pursued them.

sentences.zh: 走者糧絕，相枕而死。

translations.literal: The fugitives ran out of provisions and died piled on one another.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitives ran out of food and died in heaps.

sentences.zh: 時南州大水，百姓阻飢。

translations.literal: At that time the southern provinces suffered great floods and the people were blocked by famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year the southern provinces flooded and the people starved.

sentences.zh: 潔奏曰：「臣聞天地至公，故萬物咸育；

translations.literal: Jie memorialized, saying: "I have heard that Heaven and Earth are supremely fair, and therefore the ten thousand things all flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Jie memorialized: "I have heard that Heaven and Earth are utterly fair, and so the ten thousand things thrive;

sentences.zh: 帝王無私，而黎民戴賴。

translations.literal: the emperor is without private interest, and the black-haired people rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor has no private aim, and the people lean on him.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以神武之姿，紹重光之緒，恢隆大業，育濟羣生。

translations.literal: I bow to consider that Your Majesty, with divine martial bearing, has continued the line of restored brilliance, enlarged the great enterprise, and nourished the host of living beings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in divine martial splendor, has taken up the restored line, enlarged the great work, and nourished all life.

sentences.zh: 威之所振，無思不服，澤之所洽，無遠不懷，太平之治，於是而在。

translations.literal: Where your might has shaken, none has failed to submit; where your grace has reached, none however far has failed to cherish you — the governance of great peace is here.
translations.idiomatic: Where your might has reached, none has refused submission; where your grace has spread, none however distant has failed to turn to you—great peace is at hand.

sentences.zh: 自頃邊寇內侵，戎車屢駕，天資聖明，所在克殄。

translations.literal: In recent times border enemies have raided within; war-chariots have been driven again and again; Heaven has endowed sagely clarity, and wherever you have gone you have destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Lately border foes have raided within and chariots have rolled out again and again; Heaven has given sagely clarity, and you have crushed them wherever you marched.

sentences.zh: 方難既平，皆蒙酬錫，勳高者受爵，功卑者獲賞，寵賜優崇，有過古義。

translations.literal: Now that difficulty is settled, all have received reward; the high in merit have received ranks, the low in merit have received bounty — favor and gifts surpass the ancient norm.
translations.idiomatic: Hardship ended, all have been rewarded—high merit ennobled, low merit gifted—bounty beyond the ancients.

sentences.zh: 而郡國之民，雖不征討，服勤農桑，以供軍國，實經世之大本，府庫之所資。

translations.literal: Yet the people of the commanderies and kingdoms, though they did not join the campaigns, have toiled at farming and sericulture to supply the army and state — truly the great root of ordering the age and the resource of the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commandery folk who never marched have tilled and mulberry-fed the host and treasury—the root of rule and the storehouse's grain.

sentences.zh: 自山以東，偏遇水害，頻年不收，就食他所。

translations.literal: East of the mountains they have met with flood harm in particular; for years there has been no harvest, and they have gone elsewhere for food.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountains flood has ruined harvest after harvest, and they wander for food.

sentences.zh: 臣聞率土之濱，莫非王臣，應加哀矜，以鴻覆育。

translations.literal: I have heard that within the seas' bounds all are the king's subjects; they should receive added pity, covered and nourished like the wild goose's shade.
translations.idiomatic: Within the seas all are your subjects; pity them and shelter them as the wild goose spreads its wings.

sentences.zh: 今南摧強寇，西敗醜虜，四海晏如，人神協暢，若與兆民共饗其福。

translations.literal: Now the south has crushed a strong enemy and the west has defeated an ugly foe; within the four seas all is calm, men and spirits in harmony — if Your Majesty would share this fortune with the myriad people,
translations.idiomatic: The south has broken a strong foe, the west a vile one; within the four seas all is calm, men and spirits at ease—if Your Majesty would share this fortune with the myriad people,

sentences.zh: 則惠感和氣，蒼生悅樂矣。

translations.literal: then gracious feeling will harmonize the qi and the living will rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: grace will harmonize the qi and the living will rejoice."

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之，於是復天下一歲租賦。

translations.literal: " Shizu followed this and thereupon remitted one year's rent and tax throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu agreed and remitted one year's rent and tax throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 潔與樂平王丕督諸軍取上邽。

translations.literal: Jie with Prince of Leping Pi directed the armies to take Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Jie with Pi, Prince of Leping, led the armies to take Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 軍至啟陽，百姓爭致牛酒。

translations.literal: When the army reached Qiyang, the people vied to present cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiyang the people vied to offer cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 潔至上邽，諸將咸欲斬其豪帥以示王威，潔不聽。

translations.literal: When Jie reached Shanggui, the generals all wished to execute the clan leaders to display royal might; Jie would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanggui the generals wished to behead the clan chiefs to show royal might; Jie refused.

sentences.zh: 撫慰秦隴，秋毫無犯，人皆安業。

translations.literal: He pacified Qin and Long; not a hair was harmed, and the people all secured their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Qin and Long without harm; every household kept its livelihood.

sentences.zh: 世祖將發隴右騎卒東伐高麗。

translations.literal: Shizu was about to send the Longyou cavalry east to campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu meant to send the Longyou horse east against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 潔進曰：「隴土新民，始染大化，宜賜優復以饒實之。

translations.literal: Jie advanced and said: "The new subjects of Long are just now touched by great transformation; they should be granted generous relief to fill them out.
translations.idiomatic: Jie urged: "Long's new subjects have only just received your transformation; grant them ease and plenty.

sentences.zh: 兵馬足食，然後可用。

translations.literal: When horses and troops have full provisions, then they may be used.
translations.idiomatic: When horse and arms are fed, then use them."

sentences.zh: 」世祖深納之。

translations.literal: " Shizu deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took it deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 車駕西伐，潔為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Jie was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign Jie led the van.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍弟董來率萬餘人拒戰於城南。

translations.literal: Juqu Mujian's younger brother Donglai led more than ten thousand men to resist south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mujian's brother Donglai brought more than ten thousand to resist south of the city.

sentences.zh: 潔信卜者之言，日辰不協，擊鼓却陳，故後軍不進，董來得入城。

translations.literal: Jie trusted the diviner's words that the day and hour were inauspicious; he beat the drums and withdrew the formation, so the rear army did not advance and Donglai was able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jie trusted a diviner that the day and hour were ill-omened; he beat the drums and drew the line back, the rear did not come up, and Donglai entered the city.

sentences.zh: 世祖微嫌之。

translations.literal: Shizu was slightly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was somewhat displeased.

sentences.zh: 後潔與建寧王崇督諸軍，於三城胡部中簡兵六千，將以戍姑臧。

translations.literal: Later Jie with Prince Jianning Chong directed the armies; from the San cheng Hu tribes they selected six thousand troops to garrison Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jie with Chong, Prince Jianning, led the armies, chose six thousand from the San cheng Hu, and set them to garrison Guzang.

sentences.zh: 胡不從命，千餘人叛走。

translations.literal: The Hu did not obey orders; more than a thousand men fled in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu refused their orders, and more than a thousand men broke away in flight.

sentences.zh: 潔與崇擊誅之，虜男女數千人。

translations.literal: Jie and Chong attacked, killed them, and took captive several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Chong struck, killed them, and took several thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 潔朝夕在樞密，深見委任，性既剛直，恃寵自專。

translations.literal: Jie was morning and evening at the privy council, deeply entrusted; by nature he was sternly upright, relying on favor to act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Jie spent his days at the privy council, deeply trusted; upright by nature, he leaned on imperial favor and acted on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 世祖心稍不平。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart grew somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart turned somewhat against him.

sentences.zh: 時議伐蠕蠕，潔意不欲，言於世祖曰：「虜非有邑居，遷徙無常，前來出軍，無所擒獲，不如廣農積穀，以待其來。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of campaigning against the Rouran, Jie did not wish it and said to the emperor: "The barbarians have no settled towns; they migrate without fixed abode. In past campaigns when the army went out, nothing was captured. Better to expand farming and stockpile grain, and await their coming.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a campaign against the Rouran, Jie opposed it and told the emperor, "The barbarians have no walled towns; they wander without fixed abode. Every past expedition came back empty-handed. Better to widen the fields and heap up grain, and wait for them to come to us.

sentences.zh: 」羣臣皆從其議。

translations.literal: " The ministers all followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers all sided with him.

sentences.zh: 世祖決行，乃問於崔浩，浩固言可伐。

translations.literal: The emperor decided to go; he then asked Cui Hao, and Hao firmly said they could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resolved to march anyway and asked Cui Hao; Hao insisted they could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 世祖從浩議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Hao's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Hao's advice.

sentences.zh: 既出，與諸將期會鹿渾谷。

translations.literal: After setting out, he fixed a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army was out, he set a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.

sentences.zh: 而潔恨其計不用，欲沮諸將，乃矯詔更期，故諸將不至。

translations.literal: Jie, resenting that his plan was not used and wishing to thwart the generals, forged an edict changing the date, so the generals did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, bitter that his plan was ignored and wanting to thwart the generals, forged an edict and moved the rendezvous, so the generals never came.

sentences.zh: 時虜眾大亂，恭宗欲擊之，潔執不可，語在帝紀。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian masses were in great disorder; Crown Prince Jing wished to strike them, but Jie held that it could not be done—the matter is in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian hosts were then in turmoil; Crown Prince Jing wanted to strike, but Jie forbade it—the account is in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 停鹿渾谷六日，諸將猶不進。

translations.literal: They halted at Luhun Valley six days, yet the generals still did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They waited six days at Luhun Valley, and still the generals did not advance.

sentences.zh: [2]賊已遠遁，追至石水，不及而還。

translations.literal: [2] The bandits had already fled far; they pursued to Shishui, did not overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: [2] The enemy had already fled far off; the army chased to Shishui, failed to catch them, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 師次漠中，糧盡，士卒多死。

translations.literal: The army halted in the desert; provisions were exhausted and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted in the desert; grain ran out and many soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 潔陰使人驚軍，勸世祖棄軍輕還，世祖不從。

translations.literal: Jie secretly sent men to alarm the army and urged the emperor to abandon the army and return lightly; the emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jie secretly had men panic the troops and urged the emperor to abandon the army and ride back lightly; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 潔以軍行無功，奏歸罪於崔浩。

translations.literal: Jie, because the campaign had no success, memorialized placing blame on Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign had failed, Jie memorialized to lay the blame on Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「諸將後期，及賊不擊，罪在諸將，豈在於浩。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The generals were late, and when the bandits came they did not strike—the fault lies with the generals; how could it lie with Hao?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals were late, and when the enemy came they would not strike—the fault is the generals', not Hao's.

sentences.zh: 」浩又言潔矯詔，事遂發。

translations.literal: " Hao again spoke of Jie's forged edict, and the affair came to light.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao again exposed Jie's forged edict, and the matter broke open.

sentences.zh: 輿駕至五原，收潔幽之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan, Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan, Jie was seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 世祖之征也，潔私謂親人曰：「若軍出無功，車駕不返者，吾當立樂平王。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out on campaign, Jie had privately told his kin: "If the army goes out without success and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor marched, Jie had told his kin in private, "If the campaign fails and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.

sentences.zh: 」潔又使右丞張嵩求圖讖，問：「劉氏應王，繼國家後，我審有名姓否？

translations.literal: " Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic texts and ask: "The Liu house is fated to rule—to succeed the state thereafter; do I in truth have a name and surname?
translations.idiomatic: " Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic books and ask, "The Liu house is fated to rule and succeed the state—do I truly have a name and surname among them?

sentences.zh: 」嵩對曰：「有姓而無名。

translations.literal: " Song replied: "There is a surname but no name.
translations.idiomatic: " Song answered, "There is a surname but no name.

sentences.zh: 」窮治款引，搜嵩家，果得讖書。

translations.literal: " Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.
translations.idiomatic: " Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 潔與南康公狄隣及嵩等，皆夷三族，死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Jie, the Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred people died.

sentences.zh: 潔既居勢要，擅作威福，諸阿附者登進，[3]忤恨者黜免，內外憚之，側目而視。

translations.literal: Once Jie held a position of power, he monopolized authority and favor; those who fawned on him were promoted, [3] those who crossed him were dismissed, and within and without all feared him—men watched him sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jie held power he wielded authority and favor at will; flatterers rose, [3] the resentful were cast out, and inside and outside the court all feared him—men watched him sidelong.

sentences.zh: 拔城破國者，聚斂財貨，與潔分之。

translations.literal: Those who stormed cities and broke states heaped up wealth and goods and shared them with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Men who stormed cities and broke kingdoms heaped up loot and split it with Jie.

sentences.zh: 籍其家產，財盈巨萬。

translations.literal: When his household goods were inventoried, wealth exceeded tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: When his household was inventoried, his wealth ran to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 世祖追忿，言則切齒。

translations.literal: The emperor, in retrospective anger, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, looking back in fury, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.

sentences.zh: 古弼，代人也。

translations.literal: Gu Bi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bi came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少忠謹，好讀書，又善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he was loyal and careful, fond of reading books, and also skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was loyal and careful, loved books, and was skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初為獵郎，使長安，稱旨，轉門下奏事，以敏正著稱。

translations.literal: At first he was a hunt attendant; sent to Chang'an, he pleased the emperor and was transferred to Palace Memorials, renowned for keen uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a hunt attendant; sent to Chang'an, he pleased the throne and was moved to palace memorials, famed for sharp integrity.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，賜名曰筆，取其直而有用，後改名弼，言其輔佐材也。

translations.literal: Taizong commended him and bestowed the name Bi, taking the brush—straight and useful; later the name was changed to Bi, meaning material for assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised him and gave him the name Bi, from the writing brush—straight and useful; later the name was fixed as Bi, for one fit to assist.

sentences.zh: 令弼典西部，與劉潔等分綰機要，敷奏百揆。

translations.literal: He ordered Bi to oversee the western secretariat, sharing the pivots of state with Liu Jie and the rest and presenting memorials on the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He put Bi in charge of the western secretariat, sharing the pivots of state with Liu Jie and others and reporting on the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以功拜立節將軍，賜爵靈壽侯。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded, for merit he was made General Who Establishes Integrity and enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor succeeded, Bi was made General Who Establishes Integrity for his merit and enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 征并州叛胡。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the rebel Hu of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the rebel Hu of Bingzhou, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 還，進為侍中、吏部尚書，典南部奏事。

translations.literal: On return he was advanced to Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing, overseeing southern memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made palace attendant and director of the masters of writing, overseeing southern memorials.

sentences.zh: 與安原降東部高車於巳尼陂。

translations.literal: He also received the surrender of the eastern Gaoche at Yini Marsh with Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also received the surrender of the eastern Gaoche at Yini Marsh with Anyuan, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 又與劉潔屯五原河北，以備叛民。

translations.literal: He also camped with Liu Jie north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan to guard against rebel people.
translations.idiomatic: He also camped with Liu Jie north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan to guard against rebel subjects.

sentences.zh: 拜安西將軍，從征赫連定。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the West and followed the campaign against Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Pacifies the West and followed the campaign against Helian Ding.

sentences.zh: 駕至平涼，次于涇南。

translations.literal: When the carriage reached Pingliang, it halted south of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Pingliang, it halted south of Jing.

sentences.zh: 遣弼與侍中張黎擊平涼。

translations.literal: He sent Bi with Palace Attendant Zhang Li to attack Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bi with Palace Attendant Zhang Li to strike Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 赫連定自安定率步騎二萬來救，與弼等相遇，弼偽退以誘之。

translations.literal: Helian Ding himself led twenty thousand foot and horse from Anding to rescue; he met Bi and the rest; Bi feigned retreat to lure him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ding himself led twenty thousand foot and horse from Anding to the rescue; meeting Bi and the others, Bi feigned retreat to lure him on.

sentences.zh: 世祖使高車敕勒馳擊定，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Gaoche Tiele to charge Ding at the gallop; several thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Gaoche Tiele to charge Ding at the gallop; several thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 弼乘勝取安定。

translations.literal: Bi pressed the victory and took Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Bi pressed the victory and took Anding, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 又與永昌王健等討馮文通。

translations.literal: He also with Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and the rest campaigned against Feng Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and others in campaigning against Feng Wentong.

sentences.zh: 文通嬰城固守，弼芟其禾而還。

translations.literal: Wentong shut the city and held firm; Bi cut his grain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong shut the city and held firm; Bi cut his grain crops and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後又征文通，文通求救於高麗。

translations.literal: Later they again campaigned against Wentong; Wentong begged rescue from Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Later they campaigned against Wentong again; Wentong begged Goguryeo for rescue.

sentences.zh: 高麗救至，文通將東奔，民多難之。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo's rescue arrived, Wentong was about to flee east; the people found it hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo's rescue arrived, Wentong was about to flee east, and the people could hardly endure it.

sentences.zh: 其大臣古埿，因民心之不欲，遂率眾攻文通，開城門以引官軍。

translations.literal: His great minister Gu Lei, because the people's hearts did not wish it, then led the masses to attack Wentong and opened the city gate to bring in the official army.
translations.idiomatic: His great minister Gu Lei, seeing the people would not follow, led the masses against Wentong and opened the gates to admit the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 弼疑古埿譎詐，不入城。

translations.literal: Bi suspected Gu Lei of deceit and did not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bi suspected Gu Lei of treachery and would not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 高麗軍至，文通乃隨之。

translations.literal: When the Goguryeo army arrived, Wentong then followed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Goguryeo army arrived, Wentong went with it.

sentences.zh: 文通之奔也，令婦人被甲居中，其精卒及高麗陳兵於外。

translations.literal: When Wentong fled, he had women don armor in the center while his picked troops and the Goguryeo arrayed their soldiers outside.
translations.idiomatic: As Wentong fled, he put women in armor in the center while his picked troops and the Goguryeo drew up outside.

sentences.zh: 弼部將高苟子率騎衝擊賊軍，弼酒醉，拔刀止之，故文通得東奔。

translations.literal: Bi's subordinate general Gao Gouzi led cavalry to charge the rebel army; Bi, drunk, drew his sword to stop him, so Wentong was able to flee east.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's subordinate Gao Gouzi led cavalry to charge the rebel host; Bi, drunk, drew his sword to stop him, so Wentong escaped east.

sentences.zh: 將士皆怨弼不擊。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all resented that Bi did not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers alike resented that Bi would not strike.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒，徵還，黜為廣夏門卒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, recalled him, and demoted him to gate guard of Guangxia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, recalled him, and demoted him to gate guard of Guangxia Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋復為侍中，與尚書李順使于涼州。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made palace attendant and, with Director of the Masters of Writing Li Shun, was sent as envoy to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was palace attendant again and, with Director Li Shun, was sent as envoy to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 拜安西將軍，賜爵建興公，鎮長安，甚著威名。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing, and stationed at Chang'an with great renown.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing, and stationed at Chang'an with great renown, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 及議征涼州，弼與順咸言涼州乏水草，不宜行師。

translations.literal: When they deliberated campaigning against Liangzhou, Bi and Shun both said Liangzhou lacked grass and water and was unsuited to marching an army.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a Liangzhou campaign, Bi and Shun both said Liangzhou lacked grass and water and was no place to march an army.

sentences.zh: 世祖不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 既克姑臧，微嫌之，以其有將略，故弗之責也。

translations.literal: After Guzang was taken, he was somewhat displeased with him, but because he had generalship he did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: After Guzang fell he bore a slight grudge, yet because Bi had generalship he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣將裴方明等擊南秦王楊難當，難當遣使請救兵。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent general Pei Fangming and others to attack the Prince of Southern Qin Yang Nandang; Nandang sent envoys begging rescue troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent general Pei Fangming and others against Prince of Southern Qin Yang Nandang; Nandang sent envoys begging for rescue.

sentences.zh: 未至，難當奔上邽，方明克仇池，立楊玄庶子保熾。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Nandang fled to Shanggui; Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.
translations.idiomatic: Before relief came, Nandang fled to Shanggui; Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.

sentences.zh: 於是假弼節，督隴右諸軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi was given the staff of authority and commanded the armies of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then given the staff of authority and put in command of the armies of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣其秦州刺史胡崇之屯仇池，弼與平西將軍元齊邀崇之於濁水，臨陣擒之，其眾走還漢中。

translations.literal: Yilong sent his Qinzhou Inspector Hu Chongzhi to hold Chouchi; Bi with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Qi intercepted Chongzhi at Zhuoshui and captured him in battle; his masses fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent his Qinzhou inspector Hu Chongzhi to hold Chouchi; Bi with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Qi intercepted Chongzhi at Zhuoshui, seized him in the fight, and his troops fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 弼等從祥郊山南入，與東道將皮豹子等討仇池，遣永安侯賀純攻義隆，塞狹道。

translations.literal: Bi and the rest entered from the south of Xiangjiao Mountain with the eastern-route general Pi Baozi and the rest to campaign against Chouchi, sending Marquis of Yong'an He Chun to attack Yilong and block the narrow passes.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and the rest entered from south of Xiangjiao Mountain with eastern-route general Pi Baozi and others against Chouchi, and sent Marquis of Yong'an He Chun to strike Yilong and seal the narrow passes.

sentences.zh: 守將姜道祖退守狹亭。

translations.literal: The defending general Jiang Daozu withdrew to hold Narrow Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general Jiang Daozu fell back to hold Narrow Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 諸將以山道嶮峻，時又雪深，用馬不便，皆遲留不進。

translations.literal: The generals, because the mountain road was precipitous and at the time snow was deep so horses were inconvenient, all delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, finding the mountain road steep and snow deep so horses were useless, all hung back.

sentences.zh: 弼獨進軍，使元齊、賀純等擊狹亭，道祖南走，仇池平。

translations.literal: Bi alone advanced the army, sent Yuan Qi, He Chun, and the rest to attack Narrow Pavilion; Daozu fled south and Chouchi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bi alone pushed the army forward, sent Yuan Qi, He Chun, and the rest against Narrow Pavilion; Daozu fled south and Chouchi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸氐復推楊文德為主，圍仇池。

translations.literal: Before long the various Di again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Di clans again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 弼發上邽、高平、汧城諸軍討之，[4]仇池圍解，文德走漢川。

translations.literal: Bi sent armies from Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiansheng to campaign against them; [4] the siege of Chouchi was lifted and Wende fled to Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent armies from Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiansheng against them; [4] the siege of Chouchi was raised and Wende fled to Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 時豹子督關中諸軍次於下辨，聞仇池圍解，議欲還軍。

translations.literal: At that time Baozi commanded the Guanzhong armies and halted at Xiabian; hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, he deliberated returning the army.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi then commanded the Guanzhong armies and halted at Xiabian; hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, he debated withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 弼使謂豹子曰：「比連破賊軍，恐彼君臣未體大分，耻其負敗，或來報復。

translations.literal: Bi sent word to Baozi saying: "We have lately broken the rebel armies in succession; I fear their ruler and ministers have not yet grasped the great division, and are shamed by defeat—perhaps they will come to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent word to Baozi, "Having broken the rebel armies in succession, I fear their ruler and ministers have not yet accepted the great division and, shamed by defeat, may come for revenge.

sentences.zh: 若其班師，寇眾復至，後舉為難。

translations.literal: If you withdraw the army, the bandit masses will come again; a later effort will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: If you withdraw now, the enemy will return and a later campaign will be harder.

sentences.zh: 不如繕兵練甲，蓄力待之。

translations.literal: Better to repair arms and drill troops, store strength, and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to repair arms, drill the troops, store your strength, and wait.

sentences.zh: 不出秋冬，南寇必來，以逸待勞，百勝之策。

translations.literal: Before autumn and winter are out, the southern bandits will surely come; to await the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.
translations.idiomatic: Before autumn and winter are out the southern enemy will surely come; to meet the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.

sentences.zh: 」豹子乃止。

translations.literal: " Baozi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Baozi then held his ground.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，曰：「弼之言，長策也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and said: "Bi's words are a long-range plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he said, "Bi's words are the long view.

sentences.zh: 制南秦，弼謀多矣。」

translations.literal: In controlling Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."
translations.idiomatic: In holding Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."

sentences.zh: 恭宗總攝萬幾，徵為東宮四輔，與宜都王穆壽等並參政事。
