translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of the myriad affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and the rest in participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and others in government.

sentences.zh: 詔以弼保傅東宮，有老成之勤，賜帛千匹、綿千斤。

translations.literal: An edict made Bi tutor to the Eastern Palace; for mature, steady service he was given a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand jin of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Bi tutor to the Eastern Palace; for mature, steady service he was given a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand jin of cotton, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 弼雖事務殷湊，而讀書不輟，端謹慎密，口不言禁中之事，功名等於張黎而廉不及也。

translations.literal: Though Bi's duties were pressing, he never ceased reading; correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs; his fame and merit equaled Zhang Li's but his integrity did not.
translations.idiomatic: Though his duties pressed hard, Bi never stopped reading; correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs; his fame and merit matched Zhang Li's, but not his integrity.

sentences.zh: 上谷民上書，言苑囿過度，民無田業，乞減太半，以賜貧人。

translations.literal: People of Shanggu submitted a memorial saying the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no fields to farm, and begging to reduce them by more than half to bestow on the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Shanggu memorialized that the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no land to farm, and begged to cut them by more than half for the poor.

sentences.zh: 弼覽見之，[5]入欲陳奏，遇世祖與給事中劉樹碁，志不聽事。

translations.literal: Bi read it; [5] he entered wishing to memorialize but met the emperor playing go with Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Shu, with no mind for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi read it; [5] he entered to memorialize but found the emperor playing go with Attendant Liu Shu, with no mind for business.

sentences.zh: 弼侍坐良久，不獲申聞。

translations.literal: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not make his report heard.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not get a hearing.

sentences.zh: 乃起，於世祖前捽樹頭，掣下床，以手搏其耳，以拳毆其背曰：「朝廷不治，實爾之罪！

translations.literal: He then rose, before the emperor seized Shu's head, dragged him off the couch, struck his ears with his hand and beat his back with his fist, saying: "The court does not govern—it is truly your crime!
translations.idiomatic: He rose, seized Shu's head before the emperor, dragged him off the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, crying, "The court does not govern—and the fault is yours!

sentences.zh: 」世祖失容放碁曰：「不聽奏事，實在朕躬，樹何罪？

translations.literal: " The emperor lost composure, set down the go stones, and said: "Not to hear memorials is truly in my person—what crime has Shu?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor lost composure, set down the stones, and said, "Not hearing memorials is my fault—what crime has Shu?

sentences.zh: 置之！

translations.literal: Release him!
translations.idiomatic: Let him go!

sentences.zh: 」弼具狀以聞。

translations.literal: " Bi set forth the full circumstances in a report.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi laid the full case before him.

sentences.zh: 世祖奇弼公直，皆可其所奏，以丐百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at Bi's public uprightness and approved all he memorialized, granting it to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at Bi's blunt integrity, approved all he had urged, and granted the land to the people.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「為臣而逞其志於君前者，非無罪也。

translations.literal: Bi said: "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.

sentences.zh: 」乃詣公車，免冠徒跣，自劾請罪。

translations.literal: " He then went to the Masters of Carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself begging punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to the masters of carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself, begging punishment.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣使者召之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to summon him, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 及至，世祖曰：「卿其冠履。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor said: "Put on cap and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor said, "Put on cap and shoes.

sentences.zh: 吾聞築社之役，蹇蹷而築之，端冕而事之，神與之福。

translations.literal: I have heard that in the work of building an altar, one limps yet builds it, yet attends it in full regalia, and the spirits bless it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in building an altar one may limp yet still build it, yet attend it in full regalia—and the spirits bless it.

sentences.zh: 然則卿有何罪？

translations.literal: Then what crime have you?
translations.idiomatic: What crime have you, then?

sentences.zh: 自今以後，苟利社稷，益國便民者，雖復顛沛造次，卿則為之，無所顧也。」

translations.literal: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state, benefits the realm and eases the people—even if you are overturned and rushed—you shall do it without regard."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state and eases the people—even in overturn and haste—you shall do it without looking back."

sentences.zh: 世祖大閱，將校獵於河西。

translations.literal: The emperor held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 弼留守，詔以肥馬給騎人，弼命給弱者。

translations.literal: Bi remained on guard; an edict ordered fat horses given to the mounted men, but Bi ordered the weak ones given.
translations.idiomatic: Bi remained on guard; an edict ordered fat horses for the mounted men, but Bi gave them the weak ones.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒曰：「尖頭奴，敢裁量朕也！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "Pointed-head slave, you dare measure me!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and cried, "Pointed-head slave—you dare measure me!

sentences.zh: 朕還臺，先斬此奴。

translations.literal: When I return to the capital I will first behead this slave.
translations.idiomatic: When I return to the capital I will behead this fellow first.

sentences.zh: 」弼頭尖，世祖常名之曰筆頭，是以時人呼為筆公。

translations.literal: Bi's head was pointed; Shizu often called him Brush Head, so people called him Pen Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had a pointed head; Shizu nicknamed him Brush Head, and people called him Pen Lord.

sentences.zh: 弼屬官惶怖懼誅。

translations.literal: Bi's subordinate officials were terrified, fearing execution.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's staff were terrified they would all be executed.

sentences.zh: 弼告之曰：「吾以為事君使畋獵不適盤遊，其罪小也。

translations.literal: Bi told them: "I think that in serving one's lord, making the hunt ill-suited to roaming sport is a small fault.
translations.idiomatic: Bi told them, "Serving the throne, giving the emperor poor horses for a hunt is a small fault.

sentences.zh: 不備不虞，使戎寇恣逸，其罪大也。

translations.literal: Not preparing against the unexpected and letting barbarian raiders run free is a great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to guard against surprise and letting enemies raid at will is a grave fault.

sentences.zh: 今北狄孔熾，南虜未滅，狡焉之志，窺伺邊境，是吾憂也。

translations.literal: Now the northern Di are in full flame and the southern foes are not yet destroyed; their crafty intent watches our borders—that is my worry.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes blaze with strength and the south is not yet pacified; they watch our frontiers with hungry eyes—that is what troubles me.

sentences.zh: 故選肥馬備軍實，為不虞之遠慮。

translations.literal: Therefore I chose fat horses to stock the army and made distant provision against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: So I kept the strong horses for the army and looked far ahead against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 苟使國家有利，吾何避死乎！

translations.literal: If it profits the state, why should I shun death!
translations.idiomatic: If the realm gains by it, why should I shrink from death?

sentences.zh: 明主可以理干，此自吾罪，非卿等之咎。

translations.literal: An enlightened lord may be persuaded by reason; this fault is mine alone, not yours.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler can be reached by reason; the blame is mine, not yours.

sentences.zh: 」世祖聞而歎曰：「有臣如此，國之寶也！

translations.literal: Shizu heard and sighed: "To have a minister like this is the state's treasure!"
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard and sighed, "A minister like this is a treasure to the realm!"

sentences.zh: 」賜衣一襲、馬二匹、鹿十頭。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.
translations.idiomatic: He received a suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.

sentences.zh: 後車駕畋於山北，大獲麋鹿數千頭，詔尚書發車牛五百乘以運之。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north of the mountains and took several thousand elk and deer, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to send five hundred cart-ox teams to transport them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor hunted north of the mountains and killed thousands of elk; he ordered the secretariat to send five hundred ox-carts to haul the game.

sentences.zh: 世祖尋謂從者曰：「筆公必不與我，汝輩不如馬運之速。

translations.literal: Shizu soon told his attendants: "Pen Lord surely will not let me have them; you are not as quick as horses for hauling."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu soon told his escort, "Pen Lord will never let this pass—you are slower than horses for hauling game."

sentences.zh: 」遂還。

translations.literal: He thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back at once.

sentences.zh: 行百餘里而弼表至，曰：「今秋穀懸黃，麻菽布野，猪鹿竊食，鳥雁侵費，風波所耗，朝夕參倍，乞賜矜緩，使得收載。

translations.literal: After traveling more than a hundred li Bi's memorial arrived, saying: "Now the autumn grain hangs yellow, hemp and beans cover the wilds, pigs and deer steal the crop, birds and geese waste it, and wind and flood also consume it—the loss mounts day and night; I beg compassionate delay so it may be gathered in."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li on, Bi's memorial arrived: "Autumn grain ripens in the fields, hemp and beans cover the countryside, boar and deer devour the crop, birds waste it, and wind and flood take more still—losses double by the day; grant a stay of mercy so the harvest can be brought in."

sentences.zh: 」世祖謂左右曰：「筆公果如朕所卜，可謂社稷之臣。」

translations.literal: Shizu told those at his side: "Pen Lord is indeed as I foresaw; he may be called a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu told his attendants, "Pen Lord is just as I predicted—a true pillar of the realm."

sentences.zh: 初，楊難當之來也，詔弼悉送其子弟於京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yang Nan dang came in, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Nan dang first submitted, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.

sentences.zh: 楊玄小子文德，以黃金四十斤賂弼，弼受金，留文德而遇之無禮，文德亡入劉義隆。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan's younger son Wende bribed Bi with forty jin of gold; Bi took the gold, kept Wende, yet treated him without courtesy, and Wende fled to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan's son Wende gave Bi forty jin of gold; Bi accepted it, detained Wende, treated him roughly, and Wende fled to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其正直有戰功，弗加罪責也。

translations.literal: Shizu, because he was upright and had battle merit, did not add blame or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, weighing his uprightness and battle service, imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，吳王立，以弼為司徒。

translations.literal: When Shizu died, the Prince of Wu was established and made Bi Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu's death the Prince of Wu took the throne and made Bi minister of works.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，與張黎並坐議不合旨，俱免，有怨謗之言。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, he and Zhang Li both sat in council; their counsel did not accord with the imperial will and both were dismissed; there were words of resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, he and Zhang Li sat in council together; their advice displeased the throne and both were removed, and resentful talk followed.

sentences.zh: 其家人告巫蠱，俱伏法，時人冤之。

translations.literal: Their households reported witchcraft; both suffered execution, and people of the time deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Their families were accused of witchcraft; both were executed, and contemporaries called it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 張黎，雁門平原人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Li was a man of Pingyuan in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li was from Pingyuan in Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: [6]善書計，太祖知待之。

translations.literal: [6] Skilled in accounts, Taizu knew and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Skilled in accounts, he won Taizu's notice and favor.

sentences.zh: 太宗器其忠亮，賜爵廣平公，管綜機要。

translations.literal: Taizong valued his loyal uprightness, enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping, and put him in charge of crucial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong prized his loyal candor, made him duke of Guangping, and gave him charge of state secrets.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其功舊，任以輔弼，除大司農卿，軍國大議，黎常與焉。

translations.literal: Shizu, because of his long service and merit, employed him as a chief counselor, made him Grand Minister of Agriculture, and in great military and state deliberations Li often took part.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, honoring his long service, used him as a chief counselor and grand minister of agriculture; Li joined the weightiest military and civil deliberations.

sentences.zh: 加鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: He was further made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 以征赫連定功，進號征北大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigning against Helian Ding he was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: For campaigning against Helian Ding he was promoted to general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 與樂安王範、濟南公崔徽鎮長安，[7]清約公平，甚著聲稱。

translations.literal: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he garrisoned Chang'an, [7] frugal, fair, and of great repute.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he held Chang'an, [7] and won high repute for frugality and fairness.

sentences.zh: 代下之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he left office his house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔黎領兵一萬二千人，通莎泉道。

translations.literal: Shizu ordered Li to command twelve thousand troops and open the Shaquan route.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu ordered Li to lead twelve thousand men and open the Shaquan road.

sentences.zh: 車駕征涼州，蠕蠕吳提乘虛入寇，黎與司空道生拒擊之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned in Liangzhou, the Rouran Wuti seized the moment to invade; Li with Minister of Works Daosheng repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor campaigned in Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti struck in his absence; Li and Minister of Works Daosheng beat him back.

sentences.zh: 恭宗初總百揆，黎與東郡公崔浩等輔政，忠於奉上，非公事不言。

translations.literal: When Gongzong first took overall charge of affairs, Li with Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao and others assisted in government, loyal in serving the throne and speaking only on public business.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzong first directed government, Li with Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao and others aided the rule, loyal to the throne and speaking only on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「侍中廣平公黎、東郡公浩等，保傅東宮，有老成之勤，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Palace Attendant Duke of Guangping Li, Duke of Dongjun Hao, and others who tutor the Eastern Palace have the mature diligence of elders; We greatly commend them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Palace attendant Duke of Guangping Li, Duke of Dongjun Hao, and others who tutor the Eastern Palace show the seasoned loyalty of elders; We commend them warmly."

sentences.zh: 其賜布帛各千匹，以褒舊勳。

translations.literal: Each is granted one thousand bolts of cloth and silk to reward old merit."
translations.idiomatic: "Let each receive one thousand bolts of cloth and silk in reward for long service."

sentences.zh: 」恭宗薨於東宮，黎兼太尉，持節奉策諡焉。

translations.literal: When Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Li also held the post of Grand Commandant and, bearing the staff of office, presented the posthumous edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Li also served as grand commandant and, bearing the imperial staff, proclaimed the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 吳王余立，以黎為太尉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wu Yu was established, Li was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wu Yu was enthroned, Li was made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 後以議不合旨，免。

translations.literal: Later, because his counsel did not accord with the imperial will, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his counsel again missed the mark, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 仍與古弼並誅。

translations.literal: He was then executed together with Gu Bi.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed in the same case as Gu Bi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：和跋、奚牧、莫題、賀狄干、李栗、劉潔等，並有忠勤征伐之効，任遇仍優，俱至誅滅。

translations.literal: The historiographer writes: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, and others all had loyal, diligent merit in campaign and still received generous appointments, yet all came to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: He Ba, Xi Mu, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, Liu Jie, and the rest all fought with loyal zeal and were richly favored, yet every one was put to death.

sentences.zh: 岳見紀危難之中，受事草創之際，智勇既申，功名尤舉，乃良將之材。

translations.literal: Yue, appearing in the annals amid hardship and taking office at the founding of the state, displayed both wisdom and courage and raised his fame especially high—truly the stuff of a fine general.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, recorded in the annals through hard times and the founding crisis, showed both wit and courage and won signal fame—he was general timber of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 弼謀軍輔國，遠略正情，有柱石之量。

translations.literal: Bi counseled armies and aided the state, with far-reaching strategy and upright feeling—he had the measure of a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Bi shaped armies and steadied the state, far-sighted and upright in heart—he had the bearing of a pillar.

sentences.zh: 張黎誠謹兼方，功舊見重。

translations.literal: Zhang Li was sincere, cautious, and comprehensive in talent; his old merit won weight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, and rounded in talent; long service made him heavy in the court's eyes.

sentences.zh: 纖介之間，一朝殞覆，宥及十世，乃徒言爾，惜乎！

translations.literal: In a hair's breadth, in one morning they perished and were overthrown; "pardons reaching ten generations" was empty talk—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Between dawn and dusk they were ruined; "mercy for ten generations of kin" proved mere words—what a waste!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 擒其將狄伯支唐小方等三十餘人 北史卷二０賀狄干傳「三十」作「四十」。

translations.literal: "Captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others": in Beishi juan 20, Biography of He Digan, "thirty" reads "forty."
translations.idiomatic: "Captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than thirty others": Northern History juan 20, He Digan's life, reads thirty as forty.

sentences.zh: 按卷二太祖紀天興五年十月、卷九五姚萇傳都作「四十」，此傳「三」字訛。

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 2, Annals of Taizu, tenth month of the fifth year of Tianxing, and juan 95, Biography of Yao Chang, both read "forty"; in this biography the character "three" is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Taizu's annals, juan 2, Tianxing year 5 month 10, and juan 95, Yao Chang, both have forty; three here is corrupt.

sentences.zh: 諸將猶不進 北史卷二五劉潔傳「進」作「集」，當是。

translations.literal: "The generals still did not advance": in Beishi juan 25, Biography of Liu Jie, "advance" reads "gather"; that is likely correct.
translations.idiomatic: "The generals still did not advance": Northern History juan 25, Liu Jie's life, has advance as gather; gather is likely right.

sentences.zh: 諸阿附者登進 諸本「進」訛「長」，不可通，今據冊府卷三三八

translations.literal: "Those who fawned on him were promoted": in various editions "advance" is corrupt as "long" and will not parse; now according to Cefu juan 338
translations.idiomatic: "Those who fawned on him were promoted": editions corrupt advance as long, which will not parse; the text now follows Cefu juan 338

translations.idiomatic: folio 4000

translations.idiomatic: and is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 弼發上邽高平汧城諸軍討之 諸本「汧」作「沂」，冊府卷四二八

translations.literal: "Bi launched the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qian city to attack them": in various editions "Qian" reads "Yi"; Cefu juan 428
translations.idiomatic: "Bi launched the armies of Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qian city to attack them": editions read Qian as Yi; Cefu juan 428

translations.idiomatic: folio 5098

translations.literal: reads "Biao"; Comprehensive Mirror juan 124
translations.idiomatic: has Biao; Comprehensive Mirror juan 124

translations.idiomatic: folio 3900

sentences.zh: 作「岍」。

translations.literal: reads "Mount Qian."
translations.idiomatic: has Mount Qian.

sentences.zh: 胡注：「『岍城』意當作『汧城』。

translations.literal: Hu's note: "'Mount Qian city' in the meaning ought to read 'Qian city.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hu's note: "Mount Qian city here should be Qian city (the river-place)."

sentences.zh: 」按秦隴一帶無「沂城」，或「峅城」。

translations.literal: In the Qin-Long region there is no "Yi city," or perhaps "Biao city."
translations.idiomatic: In Qin-Long there is no Yi city; perhaps Biao city is meant.

sentences.zh: 汧城即漢汧縣故城，在今陝西隴縣，地當隴砥要道，卷四下世祖紀下太平真君六年十一月記蓋吳領導的起義軍「殺汧城守將」。

translations.literal: Qian city is the old seat of Han's Qian county, now in Long county, Shaanxi, on the key road at the Long di; juan 4, lower, Annals of Shizu, eleventh month of the sixth year of Zhenjun, records the rebel army led by Gai Wu killing the garrison commander of Qian city.
translations.idiomatic: Qian city is the old Han seat of Qian county, now in Long county, Shaanxi, on the vital Long di pass; Shizu's annals, juan 4 lower, Zhenjun year 6 month 11, record Gai Wu's rebels killing the garrison commander of Qian city.

sentences.zh: 知其地駐有軍隊。

translations.literal: This shows troops were stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: That shows a garrison was posted there.

sentences.zh: 北魏末年即在汧城設置東秦州

translations.literal: At the end of Northern Wei Eastern Qin province was established at Qian city
translations.idiomatic: Late in Northern Wei, Eastern Qin province was set up at Qian city

sentences.zh: 〈見太平寰宇記卷二九〉

translations.literal: 〈see Taiping Universal Records juan 29〉
translations.idiomatic: (see Taiping Universal Records, juan 29)
, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 「汧」是水名，「岍」是山名，皆在其地，故亦寫作「岍城」。

translations.literal: "Qian" is a river name and "Qian" a mountain name, both in that region, so it is also written "Qian city."
translations.idiomatic: The river Qian and Mount Qian both lie in that country, so the fortress is also written Qian city.

sentences.zh: 「沂」是「汧」之訛，「峅」是「岍」之訛。

translations.literal: "Yi" is a corruption of "Qian," and "Biao" a corruption of "Qian."
translations.idiomatic: Yi corrupts the river-name Qian, and Biao corrupts the mountain-name Qian.

sentences.zh: 今改「汧城」。

translations.literal: Now emended to "Qian city."
translations.idiomatic: The text is now emended to Qian city.

translations.literal: "Bi read it": Imperial Overview juan 428
translations.idiomatic: "Bi read it": Imperial Overview juan 428

translations.literal: reads "Bi read it and approved."
translations.idiomatic: has "Bi read it and approved."

sentences.zh: 按「覽」「見」重複，疑御覽是。

translations.literal: Commentary: "read" and "saw" are redundant; Imperial Overview is likely correct.
translations.idiomatic: Note: read and saw repeat; Imperial Overview is probably right.

sentences.zh: 雁門平原人也 按卷一０六上地形志上肆州雁門郡有「原平」，無「平原」。

translations.literal: "A man of Pingyuan in Yanmen": according to juan 106, upper, Monograph on Geography, upper, Sizhou, Yanmen commandery has "Yuanping" and no "Pingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: "From Pingyuan in Yanmen": Geography monograph juan 106 upper, Sizhou, Yanmen commandery, lists Yuanping and not Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 原平乃漢晉舊縣，歷見地志。

translations.literal: Yuanping was an old county of Han and Jin, recorded in successive geographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping was a Han and Jin county, recorded in every geography.

sentences.zh: 這裏「平原」當是「原平」誤倒。

translations.literal: Here "Pingyuan" should be "Yuanping" with the characters reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan here should be Yuanping with the characters reversed.

sentences.zh: 濟南公崔徽鎮長安 諸本「徽」作「徵」。

translations.literal: "Duke of Jinan Cui Hui garrisoned Chang'an": in various editions "Hui" reads "Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: "Duke of Jinan Cui Hui garrisoned Chang'an": editions read Hui as Zheng.

translations.idiomatic: Northern History juan 25, Zhang Li's life, and Cefu juan 406

translations.idiomatic: folio 4826

translations.idiomatic: have Hui.

sentences.zh: 按崔徽附卷二四崔玄伯傳，今據改。

translations.idiomatic: Note: Cui Hui is attached to juan 24, Cui Xuanbo's life; the text is emended accordingly.
